data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's criterion for distinguishing genuine reliability from compliance is the inclusion of adversarial items whose surface cues 'decouple from the underlying causal structure,' but it never supplies the causal mechanism by which the checklist itself would encode or track that causal structure. The analogy to diagnostic tests is disanalogous in exactly the causally decisive respect: a diagnostic test can be validated by a gold standard external to the test and to the test population, whereas SRC_002 itself notes that adversarial items in evaluation are constructed by 'the same process that defines genuine reliability,' risking circularity — yet it treats decoupling probes as nonetheless discriminating. It does not identify what causal feature of a checklist would let genuine reliability 'survive' decoupling probes; it simply predicts sustained accuracy. The claim conflates the causal basis of the checklist's reliability with the checklist's correlation with outcome-determining structure, but offers no mechanism explaining why a checklist that genuinely encodes causal structure would perform differently on adversarial items than one that merely tracks reliable cues. Without that mechanism, the 'if and only if' criterion is unsupported.
